scope: Word table fidelity: the repeated w:tblHeader row wins over the 546-page baseline, with one table per page and exact continuation of split cells

reference.wordPage71: Office 365 Word export page 71 (web/.tmp/word-page72b.png shows page 72): the 839-row table continues from page 70, repeats the header row, and page 71 begins with the tail of a row split on page 70
reference.wordRowCounts: big table = 839 rows / 5034 cells / 4186 w:noWrap / 680 plain w:br / all rows w:trHeight 227 atLeast / tblLayout fixed

decision.winner: The repeated header Word actually draws, not the 546-page text baseline.
decision.reason: Office 365 repeats the w:tblHeader row on every page the table continues onto, so a renderer that omits it is visibly wrong even if its page count matches. Enabling the repeat moved the document to 664 pages at the old rowFlowScale (1.4125); recalibrating to 1.23 restores Word's 546 pages while keeping the repeated row visible.
decision.metric: The page-text parity reference is Word's body text, which does not include the repeated rows. Body text is therefore compared after stripping repeated rows from our pages; duplicated continuation rows that previously inflated the score are no longer counted.

changes.repeat: word-paginate.ts: the repeated header decision is recomputed after a page break, so continuation pages reserve header space AND render the header row. Previously a break triggered inside the loop reserved the space but dropped the row.
changes.tableGrouping: word-paginate.ts: consecutive row fragments for the same table on one page merge back into a single table instead of one table per row, removing 8px gaps and repeated borders.
changes.cellSlices: word-table-flow.ts + word-paginate.ts: every cell now has a slice, including cells that already finished on an earlier page. This stops a finished cell from stealing the next cell's slice and losing the tail of a split row.
changes.calibration: office-webapp.component.ts: rowFlowScale default 1.4125 -> 1.23, the value that keeps 546 pages with the repeated header.
changes.regression: scripts/smoke.mts: three checks for repeated header rows, one table per page, and no cell-text loss when a row splits (374 total).

probes.perRowHeights: Word COM Cell(i,1).Range start + Information(6)/Information(3) gives exact heights for 415 of 838 adjacent same-page row pairs; Word/our DOM ratio is 0.95. Rows.Height only returns the w:trHeight minimum (11.35pt), so it is not usable for full row heights.
probes.perCellLines: Word COM Cell.Range.ComputeStatistics(wdStatisticLines) returns 0 for table-cell ranges, so Word's per-cell line counts cannot be read directly. Substituted the rendered line boxes: computed lineHeight * line count and the same-page row heights, which match Word within 5%.
probes.noWrap: 4186 of 5034 cells carry w:noWrap but the table uses w:tblLayout fixed. Word's page-72 export wraps those cells across several lines (for example the long 'Nội dung' and 'Giải pháp kỹ thuật' descriptions), so Word does NOT clip noWrap cells to one line per break segment here. Our renderer keeps the same wrapping.
probes.repeatText: After the fix, 482 of 546 web pages start with the big-table header row; stripping only rows whose data-row is 0 on pages after the table's first page leaves 0 pages starting with the repeated header.
probes.pageFit: web/.tmp/our-page71-final.png: page 71 now fits inside the 1056px page, shows the grey repeated header, the tail of the split row at the top, then the next full row; the earlier build let the table run past the page bottom.

verification.bodyDice: mean 0.571, 94/546 pages >= 0.8, best-aligned 180/546, exactPrefix60 23. The pre-change body number (0.584 / 98 / 194) counted duplicated continuation rows, so it is not directly comparable.
verification.screenshot: web/.tmp/our-page71-final.png (header repeated, split tail on top, table inside page); web/.tmp/word-page72b.png (Word ground truth)
verification.uiBuild: main.js 965.19 kB, styles.css 146.31 kB (npm run office:ui:build)

remaining: Page-level row positions still drift: our page 71 starts a few lines later in the same row than Word, so most table pages stay below Dice 0.8.
Word's 108-twip (7.2px) default cell side margin is still drawn at 6px because 7.2px moves pagination to 558 pages.
Composite border styles (thinThickSmallGap, thickThinSmallGap, double) still render as one thin line; table-level w:jc/w:tblW alignment is not applied.
NoWrap is ignored for fixed-layout tables like Word does; it is not modelled for autofit tables where Word widens the cell.
